missing_information_behavior: If diet and current supplement intake are unknown, do not recommend additional B6; ask for details and total intake.
safety_exclusions: Do not infer B6 deficiency from nonspecific symptoms or a broad dietary-gap goal.
Avoid chronic high-dose B6; account for all multivitamins and standalone products.
Do not treat neuropathy with B6 without clinical assessment.
professional_escalation_conditions: Tingling, numbness, burning pain, gait changes or other neurological symptoms.
Current high-dose B6 use, pregnancy, kidney disease or relevant medication use.
population_and_context: Adults concerned about dietary gaps; review actual dietary B6 intake and current products rather than infer deficiency from a general dietary-gap goal.
dose_constraints: No dose from this rule. Compare total intake with age- and jurisdiction-specific requirements and upper limits; avoid high-dose use without clinical indication.
certainty_and_limitations: NIH ODS B6 fact sheet covers intake, upper limits and peripheral neuropathy risk. A dietary-gap flag is not a diagnosis or automatic supplement indication.
